title: Linux Files, Permissions, and Users
description: A practical Linux course teaching file and directory permission bits, safe chmod, ownership concepts, and permission debugging.
goals: Interpret ls -l and ls -ld permission strings
Set minimal symbolic and numeric modes on owned files
Explain identity, ownership, group membership and root safety

notes: Do not publish until an end-to-end permission-bit verifier is implemented and tested.

Ordinary chmod lessons use only learner-owned pre-seeded Linux fixtures. The final capstone alone uses a separately authorized disposable administrator sandbox to verify the root-owned README.md (0:0) and six sandbox-owned paths; never modify host files.
Conceptual privileged/ownership lessons must not execute privileged commands.
The final capstone is one progressive project with five cumulative steps.
Teach and check parent directory traversal as well as file bits.
Only four modules: fundamentals, chmod, users/troubleshooting, and one capstone.
